rationale.conceptual: The real-space renormalization group method is an established but non-trivial technique; the specific cluster mapping, flow analysis, and phase boundary detection require careful implementation and understanding of the underlying physics, beyond a simple library call, but the paper provides sufficient detail.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of two main computational runs (finding T_c* then sweeping J2' at fixed T) with simple CSV/text outputs. Only standard Python libraries (NumPy/SciPy) are needed, and no complex orchestration, data fetching, or multi-tool integration is required.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves implementing a 20-spin real-space RG for an extended Ising model, which is a moderately complex but established method. The computational workflow has two sequential stages (T_c* determination, then J2' sweep) with straightforward I/O and standard libraries. Resource needs are trivial (CPU-only, no data).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The calculation handles a tiny 20-spin system using renormalization group on a square lattice; memory and data requirements are negligible and it runs on a single CPU core.
